# Changes from upstream sing-shadowsocks v0.2.8

- `shadowaead_2022.MultiService`: the user tables are swapped atomically by `UpdateUsers`. Upstream assigns the maps without synchronization while TCP and UDP handling read them, a data race whenever users change on a running server.
- `shadowaead_2022.MultiService.NewConnection0`: a TCP request's salt enters the replay filter only after its first chunk authenticated. Upstream recorded the salt of every connection, so anyone could grow the filter (and its periodic cleanup under a lock) without knowing a key. Replayed requests are still refused.
- `internal/udpnat` (new): a copy of sing v0.8.12's `common/udpnat` that drops a packet when its session's 64-packet queue is full instead of blocking. Every UDP service here hands packets to the NAT from the one goroutine that receives for the whole port, so upstream's blocking send let a single session whose handler was stuck (resolving a name, dialing an outbound) stop UDP for every user. `none.go`, `shadowaead` and `shadowaead_2022` (service and relay) use the copy.
- `shadowaead.Reader` / `Writer`: the 64 KiB chunk buffers are taken from sing's buffer pool when a chunk needs one and given back as soon as it is consumed or written (`Writer.Release` after the handshake header is flushed), so an idle connection holds none. Upstream allocated both per connection for its lifetime, about 150 KiB per SS2022 connection on each side. The bytes on the wire are unchanged (tested against the unpooled writer and against upstream v0.2.8 and sing-shadowsocks2 peers). Along the way: a writer now holds its lock until a sealed chunk is written, so concurrent writes can no longer send chunks out of nonce order; `WriteVectorised` flushes pending chunks before sealing a buffer longer than a chunk, instead of overwriting them; a chunk longer than the reader's maximum is an error (`ErrPacketTooLarge`) instead of a slice panic; a zero-length chunk no longer makes `ReadByte` return a stale byte.
- `shadowaead_2022` `serverConn` / `clientConn`: no `WriteVectorised`. With it, sing's copy switches to vectored reads of 8 × 64 KiB after 512 KB and keeps those buffers while the connection is idle, about 512 KiB more per connection.
- `shadowaead_2022`: padding is written as zeros (`WriteZeroN`). Upstream reserved it with `Extend`, and sing's pooled buffers are not cleared, so the padding carried whatever an earlier connection left in the buffer, encrypted to the peer: up to 900 bytes in the client's TCP request header whenever the first payload is short, and in UDP packets to or from port 53 (client and server). A third-party server, or a client of a server, could read leftover memory of the process this way.
